The season that comes after autumn is winter.

The air in the Grand Culinary Arena was thick with the scent of vanilla and anxiety. It was the final round of the National Baking Championship, and Julian, a contestant known more for his enthusiasm than his palate, stood before his cooling rack. His masterpiece: a Lemon Drizzle Cake. Or at least, it was supposed to be.

In a moment of sheer panic, Julian’s hand had trembled. He had reached for the jar labeled "Sugar" but had accidentally grabbed the identical-looking jar of "Sea Salt." The result was a cake that looked deceptively perfect but tasted like the ocean had filed a complaint against it.

Panic set in. If he presented it as is, he would be disqualified for sabotage. If he threw it away, he would be disqualified for lack of product. Julian looked at the judges, then at the other contestants, who were nervously eyeing their own creations. An idea, terrible and brilliant, struck him.

"Wait!" Julian shouted, stopping the head judge from moving to the next station. "You’re not tasting a mistake. You’re tasting a revolution."

The judges paused, spoons hovering. "A revolution?" asked Judge Elena, raising an eyebrow.

"Yes," Julian said, sweating profusely. "The 'Savory Dessert' movement. It’s all the rage in Paris. We’re challenging the notion that dessert must be sweet. We are exploring the umami depth of... lemon and salt."

The other contestants, seeing their chance to save their own slightly burnt or undercooked entries, jumped on the bandwagon. "Exactly!" cried Maria, holding up her slightly charred chocolate tart. "I’ve added a hint of smoked paprika to my ganache. It’s a 'Smoky Sweet' experience."

The room descended into chaos. One baker started sprinkling chili flakes on his macarons. Another drizzled soy sauce over his crème brûlée. The judges, bound by protocol to taste every entry, looked at each other with dawning horror.

"Very well," Judge Elena said, her voice tight. "Let us taste this... avant-garde journey."
